dataset.name: HBM Price per GB by Generation
dataset.description: HBM contract and blended pricing per GB, HBM2 through HBM4, with dated anchors from 2017 through 2026. Contract prices are confidential, so points are typed: Confirmed (source states the number), or Estimate (derived/modelled — derivation named per point). NOTE: no public HBM spot market exists in any generation — HBM sells via annual/multi-year LTAs; DRAMeXchange lists no HBM spot line. A prior spot series was retired 2026-07-28 after external verification failed.
dataset.sourceNote: Sources: TrendForce (incl. FMS 2025 blended-ASP series), TechInsights via SemiEngineering, Dealsite/Chosun Biz/Seoul Economic Daily via TrendForce News, Goldman Sachs as quoted in press, vendor IR (SK Hynix/Samsung/Micron). Contract prices are confidential; per-point typing separates stated figures from Silicon Analysts derivations. Only open-market evidence found: an isolated 2026 broker ask ~$77/GB (6-8x contract, an outlier not a market) and unpriced gray-market channels.

dataPoints.source_note: Fudzilla $80/4GB stack headline; GamersNexus multi-vendor corroboration (Kanter $150+$25). Publication date corrected to May 2017. [$80 per 4GB stack / 4 GB = $20.00/GB. GamersNexus industry sources: ~$150-160 for 8GB (2 stacks) plus ~$25 interposer, i.e. $18.75-20/GB before interposer.]

TechInsights $120/16GB stack estimate, explicitly pre-packaging; the anchor reused by later A100-era BOM analyses. [$120 / 16 GB = $7.50/GB (pre-packaging). If the stack were actually 8GB (JEDEC 4-hi ambiguity flagged by source's own wording), figure = $15.00/GB — hence wide high bound.] | Original (located 2026-09-16): Semiconductor Engineering, 2019-12-17 08:01 UTC, "What's Next For High Bandwidth Memory" by Mark LaPedus — the publication that carried the TechInsights figure, now linked instead of named. The sentence immediately after the stored one reads "That doesn’t even include the cost of the package.", which is what this point's pre-packaging basis rests on. Read against the article, two different $120 figures sit in the same paragraph on different bases: "Three years ago, HBM cost about $120/GB" (a per-GB level for ~2016) and the $120 unit price quoted here (per 16GB 4-high stack). This point uses the unit price. The article attributes the $120 to TechInsights the firm; Jeongdong Choe is quoted in the same article on HBM2E and HBM3 timing, not on the price. | Ruled 2026-09-17: attribution narrowed to the firm - the article credits the $120 to TechInsights; Jeongdong Choe is quoted on HBM2E/HBM3 timing, not on the price.

dataPoints.source_name: TrendForce (Avril Wu; press releases 2024-03-18, 2024-05-06, 2024-07-22) — revenue/bits division
dataPoints.source_note: Doubly-confirmed revenue divided by TrendForce bit chains; spread driven by which bit statement is used. [HBM 2024 revenue $18.2B (stated; also 20.1% x $90.7B DRAM = $18.2B exact cross-check) / bits 8.8-12.6B Gb (TrendForce chains) = $11.6-16.5/GB; central bits 10.7B Gb = $13.6/GB.] | Original (located 2026-09-16): TrendForce press release 2024-07-22, "Memory Industry Revenue Expected to Reach Record High in 2025 Due to Increasing Average Prices and the Rise of HBM and QLC", https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20240722-12228.html — the release that prints the $90.7B 2024 DRAM revenue this point's cross-check divides, and which separately states "HBM is expected to contribute 5% of DRAM bit shipments and 20% of revenue in 2024". The 20.1% HBM revenue share used in the cross-check is from the companion release 2024-03-18, https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20240318-12081.html ("HBM's revenue share within the DRAM industry — around 8.4% in 2023 — is projected to increase to 20.1% by the end of 2024"), and the bit-share chain from 2024-05-06, https://www.trendforce.com/presscenter/news/20240506-12125.html. What the dropped relay carried that no public TrendForce release does: the stated $18.2B 2024 HBM revenue was given by Avril Wu at TrendForce Roadshow Korea (Seoul) and reported by TweakTown on 2024-10-24, which is the date this row's source_date still names; it is not in any TrendForce press release our verifier could reach, and the public cross-check above (20.1% x $90.7B = $18.2B) is what now stands behind the figure.
dataPoints.source_excerpt: TrendForce estimates that benefiting from an increase in average DRAM prices by 53% in 2024 and 35% in 2025, DRAM revenue will reach US$90.7 billion in 2024—a 75% YoY increase—and $136.5 billion in 2025—a 51% YoY increase.

dataPoints.source_name: TrendForce (Avril Wu; news 2025-07-18, 2025-09-17) + Goldman Sachs (report not public, quoted by TrendForce) — revenue/bits division
dataPoints.source_note: Revenue/bits division. The $21.2 upper bound is a TAM-model artifact — mathematically implied by TrendForce 2025F revenue $46.7B over its lower bit chain, but a sustained $21/GB blend is BOM-implausible; retained as the honest upper bound of source disagreement (TrendForce ~30% internal bit-chain inconsistency), not a market level. Goldman $36B revenue view gives the $12.6 low. | Original (located 2026-09-16): TrendForce News 2025-07-18, "[News] HBM Prices Reportedly Face Double-digit Drop Risks in 2026, Posing Challenges for SK hynix", https://www.trendforce.com/news/2025/07/18/news-hbm-prices-reportedly-face-double-digit-drop-risks-in-2026-posing-challenges-for-sk-hynix/ — the piece that prints the Goldman Sachs $36B 2025 HBM TAM this point's $12.6 low rests on. Goldman stays a relayed source with two hops and no public document: TrendForce cites Economic Daily News (udn.com), which cites the Goldman report, so the report itself is not linkable and the clause is kept in source_name rather than replaced. The bits leg is TrendForce's own projection in TrendForce News 2025-09-17, "[News] HBM Market Heats Up as Three Giants Clash, with HBM4 at the Center", https://www.trendforce.com/news/2025/09/17/news-hbm-market-heats-up-as-three-giants-clash-with-hbm4-at-the-center/ ("TrendForce projects HBM shipments will surpass 30 billion Gb by 2026"). As with 2024, the TrendForce 2025F revenue figure this note's upper bound divides ($46.7B) was given by Avril Wu at TrendForce Roadshow Korea (Seoul) and reported by TweakTown on 2024-10-24; it is in no public TrendForce release our verifier could reach, which is part of why the $21.2 upper bound is labelled a TAM-model artifact rather than a market level.
dataPoints.source_excerpt: Goldman Sachs has revised its HBM total addressable market (TAM) estimates, raising 2025 forecast slightly by 1% to US$36 billion, but cutting 2026 outlook by 13% to US$45 billion (previously US$51 billion).

keyEvents.event_description: NVIDIA H100 ramp drives explosive HBM demand. SK Hynix sole supplier.
Capacity pre-sold via LTAs; no public HBM spot market forms (suppliers sold out for 2024 and most of 2025 — LaPedus, Jul 2024). Buyers without agreements simply cannot source.
SK Hynix CEO: "HBM sold out for 2024 and almost 2025." Extreme supply constraint.
Samsung qualifies HBM3E; SK Hynix near-monopoly starts eroding. Samsung later prices 20-30% below SK Hynix for H20 supply (Aug-Nov 2025).

Goldman's -28% 2026 HBM3E projection (Nov 2025) superseded within ~6 weeks: H200-to-China approval + ASIC demand flip 2026 renewals to ~+20% (Samsung 12-hi >+50%). Dated forecast reversal preserved in the series.
Commodity DDR5 spot per-GB exceeds HBM3E contract; DDR5 64GB RDIMM overtakes HBM in per-wafer revenue (TrendForce, Jun 2026). Suppliers seek multi-fold HBM increases for 2027.

meta.history_note: Historical HBM Price per GB by Generation data requires a free API key — anonymous callers receive the latest slice only. Get one at https://siliconanalysts.com/developers; the free tier returns a preview and Pro returns the complete time series.

freshness.cadence: Event-driven — curated prints land when a dated public source publishes one (per-dataset cadence weekly → annual, see recommended_cadence). The market-data agent sweeps Sundays 02:00 UTC; prints that clear its validation gate (source-excerpt verification included) apply automatically, the rest queue for human review.
freshness.delta_check: https://siliconanalysts.com/api/v1/changes?window=7d — the cheap way to stay current. An empty movements list means nothing moved past its significance threshold: that is signal, not staleness. CoWoS capacity, foundry utilization, node-ramp, HBM bit-share and HBM bonding-yield signals have not been collected since the 2026-10-26 run (the weekly capacity refresh is paused), so no movement is detected for them.
